c_swap_temp.learningObjective: Learn variable value swapping using a third temporary memory slot in C.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Allocate integers: a = 10, b = 20, temp = uninitialized.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Memory me a = 10, b = 20 aur temp allocate hue.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: temp = a; Backup value of a (10) into temp slot.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: temp = a; a ki value (10) temp variable me copy ho gayi.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: a = b; Overwrite a with b's value (20).
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: a = b; a ke andar b ki value (20) overwrite ho gayi.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: b = temp; Transfer original value of a (10) from temp into b.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: b = temp; temp me rakhi puraani value (10) ab b me aa gayi. Swapping complete!

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: printf prints swapped values: a=20, b=10.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: printf se console pe a=20, b=10 output display hua.

c_swap_no_temp.learningObjective: Swap two variables using arithmetic addition and subtraction without extra memory.

executionSteps.explanationHinglish: a = 15 aur b = 30 declare hue.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: a = a + b; Combine both numbers: 15 + 30 = 45.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: a = a + b; dono ka sum (15 + 30 = 45) a me store hua.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: b = a - b; Extract original a: 45 - 30 = 15. Now b holds 15!
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: b = a - b; sum me se b subtract kiya (45 - 30 = 15). Ab b = 15 ban gaya!

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: a = a - b; Extract original b: 45 - 15 = 30. Swapping complete!
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: a = a - b; sum me se naya b subtract kiya (45 - 15 = 30). Swapping ho gayi!

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: printf prints swapped values: a=30, b=15.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: printf se console pe a=30, b=15 print hua.

c_constants.learningObjective: Understand how const locks memory from modification compared to normal variables in C.

tokens.value: // MAX_LIMIT = 150; // ERROR! const variable cannot be modified

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Declare mutable variable: int score = 50 [Read/Write RAM].
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Normal variable 'score' = 50 declare hua. Iski value future me badal sakti hai.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Declare constant: const int MAX_LIMIT = 100 [LOCKED / Read-Only Memory].
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: const int MAX_LIMIT = 100 declare hua. 'const' lagane se ye box LOCK (Read-Only) ho gaya!

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: score = 75; Modification ALLOWED because 'score' is a normal variable (50 → 75).
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: score = 75; Success! score normal variable hai isliye iski value change hokar 75 ho gayi.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Attempting MAX_LIMIT = 150 would cause COMPILER ERROR: "assignment of read-only variable 'MAX_LIMIT'".
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Agar hum MAX_LIMIT = 150 likhenge toh C Compiler ERROR dega: "assignment of read-only variable". Constant kabhi change nahi ho sakta!

animationEvent.explanation: ERROR: Cannot assign to variable with const-qualified type

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: printf prints final values: Score: 75, Max: 100.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: printf se console pe Score: 75, Max: 100 print hua.

c_arithmetic.learningObjective: Demonstrate all 5 C arithmetic operators (+, -, *, /, %) with integer division vs modulo.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Declare inputs: int a = 20, int b = 6.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Operands a = 20 aur b = 6 declare hue.
Addition: sum = 20 + 6 = 26.
Subtraction: diff = 20 - 6 = 14.
Multiplication: prod = 20 * 6 = 120.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Integer Division: quot = a / b = 20 / 6 = 3 (discards decimals).
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Integer Division: quot = 20 / 6 = 3 (C me fractional part cut ho jata hai).
Modulo Operator: rem = 20 % 6 = 2 (division ke baad bacha remainder).
printf se sabhi arithmetic calculations console pe display hue.

c_relational_logical.learningObjective: Evaluate relational comparisons and logical compound conditions (AND, OR, NOT) in C.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Declare integers: x = 10, y = 25. In C, boolean TRUE is 1 and FALSE is 0.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: x = 10 aur y = 25 declare hue. C me TRUE ka matlab 1 aur FALSE ka matlab 0 hota hai.
Relational (<): (10 < 25) ka result 1 (TRUE) mila.
Relational (==): (10 == 25) equality check hua → result 0.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Logical AND (&&): (10 > 0 && 25 > 20) evaluates to 1. Both conditions must be TRUE.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Logical AND (&&): dono conditions check hui → result 1.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Logical OR (||): (10 == 0 || 25 > 0) evaluates to 1. At least one condition must be TRUE.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Logical OR (||): koi ek condition TRUE hone par result 1 hota hai → result 1.
Logical NOT (!): result invert ho gaya → 1.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: printf prints all relational & logical results: <:1, ==:0, &&:1, ||:1, !:1.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: printf se console pe sabhi condition results display hue.

c_inc_dec.learningObjective: Master prefix vs postfix increment and decrement memory evaluation timing in C.

tokens.value: // Step 1: x increments to 6, Step 2: pre gets 6
// Step 1: post gets old 5, Step 2: y increments to 6

executionSteps.explanationHinglish: x = 5 aur y = 5 initialize hue.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: PRE-INCREMENT (++x): 1. Memory increments x from 5 to 6 first. 2. Value 6 is assigned to pre.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: PRE-INCREMENT (++x): Pehle x ki value badhkar 6 hui, phir wahi nayi value (6) 'pre' me store hui.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: POST-INCREMENT (y++): 1. Current value 5 is assigned to post first. 2. Then y increments in memory to 6.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: POST-INCREMENT (y++): Pehle puraani value (5) 'post' ko mili, uske baad y memory me badhkar 6 hua.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: printf shows the difference: pre=6 (x=6), post=5 (y=6).
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: printf se clear hua: pre=6 aur post=5.

c_temp_converter.learningObjective: Master operator precedence and float conversion formula (F = (C * 9/5) + 32) in C.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Convert: (25 * 9.0 / 5.0) + 32.0 = 77.0 °F. Note: Using 9.0/5.0 prevents integer truncation (9/5 would be 1).

c_scanf_integer.learningObjective: Master user input in C using scanf with format specifier %d and address-of operator (&).

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Declare integer variable 'num' [4 Bytes] in memory (currently holds uninitialized garbage).
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Integer variable 'num' [4 Bytes] memory me declare hua (abhi uninitialized hai).

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: printf displays console prompt: "Enter an integer: ".
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: printf ne console pe message show kiya: "Enter an integer: ".

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: User inputs "42". scanf filters it via '%d' and writes integer 42 directly into memory address &num (0x7ffd4).
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: User ne "42" type kiya. scanf ne '%d' filter se parse karke memory address &num (0x7ffd4) pe store kar diya.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: printf reads value from 'num' and formats with '%d' to output: You entered: 42.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: printf ne '%d' specifier se num ki value read karke console pe print kar di: You entered: 42.

c_scanf_string.learningObjective: Understand how scanf with %s reads words into a char array and automatically adds null-terminator (\0).

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Declare character array 'name[20]' [20 Bytes]. In C, arrays act as direct memory pointers.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Character array 'name[20]' [20 Bytes] allocate hua. C me array name khud ek memory address hota hai.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: printf prints "Enter your name: " on terminal.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: printf se terminal pe "Enter your name: " message display hua.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: scanf reads string "Alex" via '%s'. Notice no '&' needed because array 'name' already decays to base address (0x7ffe0). It appends '\0' at the end.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: scanf '%s' se string "Alex" read karta hai. Array name already base address (0x7ffe0) hai isliye '&' ki zaroorat nahi hoti. End me '\0' automatically lag jata hai.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: printf with '%s' traverses characters from memory until it finds '\0' sentinel: Hello, Alex!
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: printf '%s' memory me se characters read karke jab tak '\0' na mile print karta hai: Hello, Alex!

c_implicit_casting.learningObjective: Understand automatic widening conversion where C safely promotes int (4B) to double (8B) without precision loss.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Declare integer variable: int count = 42 [4 Bytes].
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Integer variable 'count' = 42 [4 Bytes] memory me allocate hua.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Implicit Type Promotion: C automatically converts integer 42 [4 Bytes] to double 42.00 [8 Bytes] without data loss.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Automatic Widening: C ne integer 42 [4B] ko bina kisi loss ke double 42.00 [8B] me promote kar diya.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: printf prints both original int and promoted double: int: 42, double: 42.00.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: printf se console pe int: 42 aur double: 42.00 display hua.

executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Double price = 99.75 memory me declare hua.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Explicit Cast (int)price: C forcibly truncates fractional part (.75) $\rightarrow$ stores integer 99 in 4-byte box.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: printf shows truncated result: double: 99.75 -> int: 99.
